Name: C Stuart Hardwick
Question: Doesn’t new life need inherited genetic material from parents such as DNA and chromosomes? How does abiogenesis life from death work?
Answer: Not to get started, no. The sophisticated heritable genetics used by life today is needed to evolve complex forms, but the only requirement for evolution to happen is that it can replicate and that the replication is not quite perfect. You don’t need genes for that. and as long as that’s true (and nothing gets in the way of it) evolution is a logically unavoidable result. Simple lipid microspheres can spontaneously arise and self replicate in conditions so simple, they can be set up in a high school chemistry lab and would certainly have existed on the early Earth. The chemistry is no more complicated that that behind soap bubbles, and the result is not essentially different from the membrane of a living cell—its just simpler and less stable. And remember, genes are not computer programs. Ultimately DNA is mostly just a shape template for RNA, which is a shape template for proteins. Today, there’s a lot of machinery around it that helps turn those proteins into structure and enzymes into action, but ultimately, all of it boils down to influencing chemistry to do basically what it does anyway. On a planet devoid of life but possessing the right conditions, trillions upon trillions of self-replicating lipid microspheres are eventually doing to stumble upon a contaminant that makes them more stable in some way, and no matter how small that change is, it will quickly dominate. Meanwhile, RNA molecules can also self-assemble and then “self-catalyze” a fancy way of saying they make copies of themselves. Amino acids, lipids, and sugar can form inorganically through a variety of means, and all offer useful components to any evolving proto-life. There are a lot of simpler steps between microspheres and what we consider “true” cells, but it take remarkable recalcitrant to pretend that, given the opportunity, those steps are not a necessary consequence of chemistry and ultimately physics. Life is ubiquitous in the universe. You can take that to the bank. We may never know that exact steps by which it arose on Earth, but that such steps can and must occur anywhere in the universe conditions allow is absolutely clear.

Name: C Stuart Hardwick
Question: Is there a way to calculate how many more nuclear power plants America will need to supply enough electricity to eliminate the internal combustion engine? Could it be in the hundreds?
Answer: Sure: According to the U.S. Department of Energy, the transportation sector consumes about 27.82 quadrillion BTUs per year, or 8.15 × 10^12 kWh. EVs are 3–4 times more energy efficient than IC vehicles, so we’d really need more like 2.3 × 10^12 kWh. To meet the additional demand, we’d need 266 new 1GW nuclear power plants, plus quite a but of new power grid infrastructure. That sounds like a lot, until you know we already have 7,000 power plants of various types, then not so much. Of course, a more realistic proposal is to expand along the lines of the current mix of nuclear with wind, solar, hydro, and other sources, in which case we would only need about 66 new nuclear plants. And for that, we would eliminate American economic dependence on foreign oil, eliminate the single largest global cause of war, and eliminate one major source of North American ground level air-pollution and respiratory illness. And if we take a smarter approach and build not only the full 266 nuclear plants but enough additional plants to displace all remaining coal fired plants, we would make a sizeable dent on global greenhouse gas emission and eliminate a source of roughly 50,000 premature pollution-related deaths each year in the U.S. alone. And if we were really, really smart—like Montreal Accords level smart—we’d build an additional hundred or so plants located far from existing demand, just to produce power for use in extracting carbon from the atmosphere for geologic sequestration in the form of carbonate rock, and that would be enough to non-trivially slow global warming and ocean acidification. But none of this is going to happen because the American people are so profoundly ignorant, we are a people convinced that the safest, cleanest source of power ever devised is actually filthier and more dangerous than all the others. One is tempted to roll one’s eyes and dream of planetary escape through alien abduction.

Humans aren’t the strongest, the biggest, or fastest, nor are we anythings remotely like god-like perfection.
